title: Nightcap observability triage log - Rylie
content:
2026-03-12 nightcap log (quick, messy)
Context: On-call kickover at 22:00. Customer reported dashboard heatmap showing stale usage counts after midnight (timezone confusion?). Low-sev for customer, but reproducible and confusing for internal dashboards.

Quick timeline:
- 21:50: alert from pagerduty: metrics-delay-high (team: obs).
- 22:05: joined #obs-triage; saw customer screenshot (heatmap 00:00-01:00 all zeros).
- 22:12: confirmed internal dashboards (prod, region-us-west) show same zeros for that window.
- 22:25: created JIRA INF-4217 and started root-cause probe.
- 23:00: rolled back a small config change to metrics-collector (temp revert) — no change.
- 23:30: confirmed that raw ingestion (kafka topic: telemetry-raw) has events for that time window, so ingestion upstream is ok.
- 23:50: discovered that the dashboard heatmap query applies a timezone floor() incorrectly when rollup=hour and tz param absent; likely edge-case when daylight savings or midnight boundary triggers rounding to the wrong day.

Immediate repro steps I used (notes to self):
1) Curl the API that backfills rollups: curl -s -u :$TOKEN "https://metrics.redwood.internal/api/v1/rollups?metric=active_tokens&from=2026-03-12T00:00:00Z&to=2026-03-12T02:00:00Z&rollup=hour" - look at payload - had zeros for 00:00 bucket.
2) Check kafka offsets for telemetry-raw: kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --group rollup-consumer - confirmed offsets > 00:00 events present.
3) Run local Grafana query used by the heatmap and toggle tz param (timezone=UTC vs local): found difference.
4) Run small python script to emulate rollup floor logic: observed off-by-one hour when tz arg dropped.

Hypothesis: rollup service (consumer v1.6.3) relies on OS timezone env in one code path; when a day-rollover hits near midnight UTC/local mismatch, the aggregation bucket becomes empty for the UI window even though raw events exist. There was a recent patch (PR #1289) that changed default timezone fallback — maybe introduced a regression for requests that do not explicitly include timezone.

Notes for follow-ups (prioritized):
- HIGH: Add tz param to heatmap queries in console frontend as a band-aid (fast). (Owner: Rylie)
- HIGH: Add unit test for rollup floor logic in consumer service to cover midnight boundary cases (Owner: eng-serving-runtime or whoever owns rollups). Patch likely in PR #1289.
- MEDIUM: Instrument rollup service to log tz resolution path and the chosen tz for each aggregation job (low-cost, helps postmortem).
- MEDIUM: Add dashboard lint that flags queries without explicit timezone at build-time.
- LOW: Longer-term refactor to centralize timezone handling in metrics platform.

Open questions (to resolve tomorrow):
- Did any Dedicated or Private customers see the same effect? (ask CS for reported incidents)
- Was there any scheduled maintenance around 2026-03-12 00:00 UTC that could have toggled env tz? (check infra calendar)
- Should we backfill users who saw zeros? Might be a customer-impact rollback scope decision.

Quick scratch TODOs (ordered quick wins):
- [x] Post initial triage note in #obs-triage (22:30)
- [x] Create JIRA INF-4217 and link artifacts (22:45)
- [x] Revert small config change (22:55)
- [ ] Patch console frontend to include tz in heatmap queries (estimate 1-2 hrs)
- [ ] Draft quick runbook entry: "midnight heatmap zeros" (estimate 30m)
- [ ] Add unit test + CI job for rollup boundary case (owner: rollup-service)

Observability snippets / queries I ran (copyable):
- Grafana panel query (heatmap): SELECT date_trunc('hour', sample_ts AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AT TIME ZONE $tz) AS bucket, count(*) FROM metrics_events WHERE sample_ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
- Kafka check: kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --group rollup-consumer | grep 2026-03-12
- Curl rollup API: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://metrics.redwood.internal/api/v1/rollups?metric=active_tokens&from=2026-03-12T00:00:00Z&to=2026-03-12T03:00:00Z&rollup=hour" | jq .

Hand-off notes for morning shift (add to JIRA description):
- Root cause likely timezone fallback regression introduced in PR #1289.
- Fast mitigation: force tz query param from frontend for heatmap routes + add logging.
- Data integrity: raw events are present; aggregation path produced zeros due to bucket miscalc. No need for raw ingestion reprocessing at this time; prioritize stability and tests.

Personal notes to self:
- Keep the morning follow-up tight: get a simple console patch out first (avoid rabbit holes).
- Remind platform team to include timezone unit tests when touching date math.
- Sleep.

End of nightcap log.
